name: Cricket
desc: Cricket is a bat-and-ball game on a big oval field. One team bats and scores runs while the other bowls and fields, trying to get the batters out.
howTo: Split into two teams. One team bats first; the other bowls and fields.
The bowler throws the ball at the wicket. The batter hits it and runs to the other end to score a run.
Hit the ball to the fence for 4 runs. Hit it over the fence for 6!
Fielders try to catch the ball or hit the wicket before the runner gets there.
When batters are out, the teams swap. The team with more runs wins.
rules: A team's turn to bat ends after a fixed number of balls or when 10 batters are out.
The bowler must throw the ball with a straight arm.
If the ball hits the wicket, the batter is out — this is called bowled.
If a fielder catches the ball before it touches the ground, the batter is out.
Batters must stay behind the crease line when running.
The team with the most runs at the end wins.
fact: The longest Test cricket matches last 5 days — and can still end with no winner at all!

name: Football
desc: Football (soccer) is the world's most popular game. Two teams kick a ball and try to score goals — and only the goalkeeper may use their hands.
howTo: Two teams of 11 play on a grass field with a goal at each end.
Dribble the ball with your feet and pass it to your teammates.
Kick the ball into the other team's goal to score 1 point.
Only the goalkeeper may use hands — and only inside the penalty box.
Play two halves of 45 minutes. The team with more goals wins.
rules: No touching the ball with hands or arms — except the goalkeeper.
No pushing, tripping or kicking other players. That is a foul.
A foul inside your own penalty box gives the other team a penalty kick.
If the ball goes out on the side line, the other team throws it back in.
If the ball goes out behind the goal line, it is a corner kick or a goal kick.
fact: The FIFA World Cup final is the most-watched sports event on Earth — more than a billion people tune in.

name: Basketball
desc: Basketball is a fast game on a court with a hoop at each end. Teams dribble, pass and shoot the ball to score points.
howTo: Five players from each team are on the court at one time.
Move the ball by dribbling (bouncing it) or passing to a teammate.
Shoot the ball through the hoop for 2 points, or 3 points from far away.
If you stop dribbling, you must pass or shoot — you cannot run with the ball.
After a basket, the other team gets the ball. Most points at the end wins.
rules: You must dribble while running with the ball. Running without dribbling is called travelling.
You cannot push, hold or block with your body — that is a foul.
A free throw is given after some fouls and scores 1 point.
A game has four quarters. Teams swap ends after each one.
The team with the most points when time runs out wins.
fact: The first hoops were real peach baskets — someone had to climb a ladder to fetch the ball after every single basket!

name: Baseball
desc: Baseball is a bat-and-ball game on a diamond-shaped field. The batter hits the ball and runs around four bases to score.
howTo: One team bats while the other team fields.
The pitcher throws the ball and the batter tries to hit it.
Run to first base, then second, third and back to home plate to score a run.
Fielders catch the ball or tag the runner to get them out.
Three outs and the teams swap. After 9 innings, most runs wins.
rules: A batter is out if a fielder catches the ball before it touches the ground.
Three strikes (swings and misses) and the batter is out.
Four wide throws (balls) let the batter walk to first base for free.
A home run is a hit that flies over the fence — everyone on base scores too.
Runners must touch every base in order.
fact: In Japan, baseball is so loved that the high school tournament is broadcast across the whole country.

name: American Football
desc: American football is a tough team game with an oval ball. Teams march down the field to reach the end zone and score a touchdown.
howTo: The attacking team gets four tries (downs) to move the ball 10 yards forward.
Run with the ball or throw a pass to a teammate to gain yards.
Reach the end zone for a touchdown — 6 points, plus a bonus kick for 1 more.
Make 10 yards and you get four fresh tries. Fail, and the other team gets the ball.
The team with the most points when time runs out wins.
rules: You may throw the ball forward only once per play, from behind the line.
Tackling is allowed — that is why players wear helmets and pads.
Play stops when the player with the ball is tackled to the ground.
A field goal kick through the tall posts scores 3 points.
The ball is dead if it touches the ground after a forward pass.
fact: The Super Bowl is famous for its giant halftime show — and for funny ads that cost millions of dollars for 30 seconds.

name: Ice Hockey
desc: Ice hockey is played on ice at lightning speed. Skaters use sticks to shoot a hard rubber puck into the other team's net.
howTo: Six players from each team skate on the ice, including one goalie.
Pass the puck with your stick and skate it toward the other net.
Shoot the puck into the net to score a goal.
Teams swap players on the fly — even mid-play — to stay fresh.
Three periods of 20 minutes. The most goals wins.
rules: You may bump players against the boards, but no tripping or slashing with the stick.
The puck must cross the goal line fully for the goal to count.
Rough play sends a player to the penalty box for a few minutes.
The goalie may use hands, stick and pads to stop the puck.
If the score is tied, an exciting shootout decides the winner.
fact: Canada gave the world ice hockey — kids there learn to skate almost as soon as they can walk.

name: Field Hockey
desc: Field hockey is one of the oldest team games on Earth. Players use curved sticks to dribble and hit a small hard ball into the goal.
howTo: Two teams of 11 play on grass or turf.
Only the flat side of the stick may touch the ball.
Dribble, pass and push the ball up the field.
Shoot the ball into the goal to score a point.
Two halves of 35 minutes — most goals wins.
rules: Only the flat side of the stick may touch the ball, never the rounded side.
You may not raise your stick above shoulder height.
If the ball touches your foot, the other team gets a free hit.
Dangerous play gives the other team a penalty corner.
The goalkeeper may use any part of the body to stop the ball.
fact: A 4,000-year-old carving from ancient Greece shows people playing a stick-and-ball game that looks a lot like hockey.

name: Volleyball
desc: Volleyball is played over a high net. Teams hit the ball with their hands and must never let it touch the ground.
howTo: Six players stand on each side of the net.
Serve the ball over the net to start play.
Each team may touch the ball up to 3 times before sending it back.
Spike the ball down or block it at the net to win the rally.
Win 3 sets of 25 points to take the match.
rules: You cannot catch or hold the ball — it must be hit, not thrown.
One player may not touch the ball twice in a row (except after a block).
If the ball lands on the ground on your side, the other team scores.
Players rotate one spot clockwise each time their team wins back the serve.
Reaching over the net to touch the ball is not allowed.
fact: Volleyball is Sri Lanka's national sport — villages there have played it for over a hundred years.

name: Rugby
desc: Rugby is a full-contact game with an oval ball. Teams carry, pass and kick the ball to score tries at the other end.
howTo: Carry the ball forward by running with it.
Pass the ball only backwards or sideways — never forward.
Kick the ball ahead and chase it to gain ground.
Press the ball down in the other team's end zone to score a try — 5 points.
After a try, kick the ball over the crossbar for 2 extra points.
rules: Forward passes are not allowed — pass backwards or kick ahead.
Tackling the ball carrier is allowed, but always tackle low.
Only standing players may join a ruck, and they must come from their own side.
A penalty or drop kick through the posts scores 3 points.
The team with more points after 80 minutes wins.
fact: New Zealand's All Blacks perform the haka — a fierce Māori war dance — before every match, and it gives millions goosebumps.

name: Badminton
desc: Badminton is the fastest racquet sport in the world. Players tap a feathered shuttlecock back and forth over a high net.
howTo: Serve underhand, from below your waist, to start the rally.
Hit the shuttle with light taps or powerful smashes.
Land the shuttle inside the other court to win the rally.
Play singles (1 vs 1) or doubles (2 vs 2).
First to 21 points wins the game — win 2 games to take the match.
rules: You must serve underhand, from below your waist.
The shuttle may be hit only once before it crosses the net.
If the shuttle touches the ground, the rally is over.
Points are scored on every rally, no matter who served.
At 20-20 you need a 2-point lead to win the game.
fact: Smashes in badminton can fly over 400 km/h — faster than a Formula 1 car!

name: Table Tennis
desc: Table tennis (ping pong) is a lightning-fast game on a small table — and China treats it like a national treasure.
howTo: Serve by tossing the ball and hitting it so it bounces on both sides of the table.
Return the ball after exactly one bounce on your side.
Spin the ball with your paddle to make it swerve and jump.
Win the rally when the other player misses or hits the net.
First to 11 points wins — but you need a 2-point lead.
rules: A serve must bounce once on each side of the table.
You cannot hit the ball before it bounces on your side.
If the ball clips the net and lands over on a serve, it is a let — serve again.
Serve changes hands every 2 points.
Players swap ends of the table after every game.
fact: China's table tennis teams have won most of the Olympic gold medals ever awarded for the sport.

name: Kabaddi
gear: Just a mat or open ground
desc: Kabaddi is an exciting chasing game from India — no ball, no gear, just lung power. The raider chants 'kabaddi, kabaddi' without taking a breath!
howTo: Two teams of 7 sit on opposite halves of the court.
One raider runs into the other half, chanting 'kabaddi, kabaddi' in one breath.
The raider tries to touch a defender and run back home.
Defenders grab and hold the raider to stop them escaping.
A touch scores 1 point for the raiders; a tackle scores 1 for the defenders.
rules: The raider must keep chanting and return home in one breath.
If the raider breathes in before returning, they are out.
Defenders may not cross the centre line.
A raider is out if defenders hold them until they take a breath.
Most points after two 20-minute halves wins.
fact: Kabaddi is the national sport of Bangladesh, and India has won almost every Kabaddi World Cup ever played.

name: Kho-Kho
desc: Kho-Kho is India's classic chasing game, full of sprinting and dodging. Chasers kneel in a row in the middle and chase runners in turns.
howTo: Nine chasers kneel in a line; runners dodge around them.
The active chaser runs to tag a runner with their hand.
Chasers pass the turn by touching a seated teammate's back and shouting 'kho'!
The new chaser must run the other way around the row.
Tag all the runners in the shortest time to win.
rules: A chaser may only change direction by going around the row of seated players.
The turn passes only with a touch and a shout of 'kho'.
Runners may not cross the middle line or leave the field.
A tag only counts with the hand, never the feet.
Each chase turn lasts a fixed time — usually 9 minutes.
fact: Kho-Kho has been played on school grounds across India for generations — it is one of the oldest tag games in the country.

name: Gilli Danda
desc: Gilli Danda is an ancient Indian street game — cricket's great-grandfather. Flick a small wooden peg (gilli) with a big stick (danda) and send it flying.
howTo: Dig a small oval hole in the ground and lay the gilli across it.
Slide the danda into the hole to flick the gilli up into the air.
Strike the airborne gilli as far as you can with the danda.
Run to a marked point and back while the fielders chase the gilli.
Score points for distance — but if a fielder catches the gilli, you are out.
rules: The batter gets three tries to flick the gilli into the air.
If the gilli lands on the hole or right next to it, the batter is out.
Fielders may catch the gilli mid-air to get the batter out.
Points are counted in danda-lengths — the farther it flies, the more you score.
Every player on the team gets a turn to bat.
fact: Gilli Danda is over 2,500 years old and is played across South Asia under many local names.

name: Lagori
desc: Lagori (also called Pithoo or Satoliya) is a storming-and-stacking game. Knock down a tower of stones, then rebuild it before the other team hits you with the ball.
howTo: Stack 7 flat stones into a small tower.
Team 1 knocks the tower down by throwing the ball.
Team 1 now tries to restack the stones while Team 2 throws the ball at them.
If the ball touches a player, that player is out.
Restack all 7 stones and shout 'Lagori!' to win the round — then teams swap.
rules: Team 2 gets the ball as soon as the tower falls.
If the ball touches a restacking player, that player is out.
Players may dodge but must stay inside the playing area.
The round ends when the tower is rebuilt or all restackers are out.
Teams swap roles after every round.
fact: Lagori has a different name in almost every Indian state — Pithoo, Satoliya, Dikori and many more.

name: Sumo
desc: Sumo is Japan's national sport — a giant wrestling duel in a clay ring. Push your opponent out, or make them touch the ground.
howTo: Two wrestlers face each other in a round clay ring.
Squat, glare, and charge when the moment is right.
Push, shove and grip the opponent's belt (mawashi).
Force the opponent out of the ring or onto the ground.
The winner takes the bout — matches often last only seconds!
rules: You lose if any part of you except the soles of your feet touches the ground.
You lose if any part of you steps outside the ring.
Punching, kicking and hair-pulling are strictly banned.
The referee (gyoji) waves a fan to declare the winner.
Wrestlers follow ancient rituals before every bout — like throwing salt to purify the ring.
fact: Sumo wrestlers can weigh as much as 200 kilograms — yet top champions are so flexible that many can do the splits!

name: Sepak Takraw
desc: Sepak takraw is volleyball's wild Southeast Asian cousin — but no hands allowed! Players kick, knee and head the ball over the net.
howTo: Three players stand on each side of the net.
Serve with your foot — kick the ball over the net.
Each team gets up to 3 touches to send the ball back.
Use feet, knees, chest or head — never hands or arms.
Win 3 sets of 21 points to take the match.
rules: Hands and arms are strictly off-limits.
Each team may touch the ball at most 3 times between crosses.
The ball must not touch the ground on your side.
You need a 2-point lead to win a set.
The same player may not touch the ball twice in a row.
fact: The 'sunback spike' is a flying somersault kick that smashes the ball over the net at over 140 km/h!

name: Taekwondo
desc: Taekwondo is Korea's national martial art — 'the way of the foot and fist'. Fighters score with fast, high kicks on padded targets.
howTo: Two fighters bow and face each other on a padded mat.
Score points by kicking the opponent's body protector or head.
A body kick scores 1; spinning kicks and head kicks score more.
Land more scoring hits than your opponent in three rounds.
Bow after the match — respect comes first.
rules: Punches to the head and kicks below the belt are banned.
Pushing, grabbing and falling on purpose cost points.
Fighters wear padded guards, helmets and mouthguards.
A match has three rounds of 2 minutes each.
Fighters bow before and after every match.
fact: Over 70 million people practise taekwondo in more than 200 countries — it is one of the most popular martial arts ever.

name: Chess
desc: Chess is the world's most famous board game — a battle of two armies on 64 squares. Trap the enemy king to win.
howTo: Set the board so each player has a light square at the bottom-right corner.
White moves first, then players take turns — one move each.
Each piece moves its own way: rooks straight, bishops slanting, knights in an L.
Capture enemy pieces by landing on their square.
Trap the enemy king so it cannot escape — that is checkmate, and the win.
rules: You may never put your own king in danger.
When your king is attacked it is 'check' — you must respond at once.
Pawns move forward but capture diagonally.
A pawn may move two squares on its first move — and becomes a queen if it reaches the far end.
The game can end in a draw when neither player can win.
fact: Chess was born in India over 1,500 years ago as a game called chaturanga — the queen only became the strongest piece a few hundred years ago.

name: Carrom
desc: Carrom is India's beloved flick-and-pocket game — like finger billiards. Flick the striker to sink all your coins into the corner pockets.
howTo: Sit facing each other with the board between you.
Flick the striker with your finger from your baseline.
Pocket your colour of coins — white or black.
Pocket the red queen, then 'cover' it by pocketing your own coin next.
Sink all nine of your coins to win the board.
rules: Flick the striker only forward from your baseline.
If you pocket the striker, one of your sunk coins goes back to the centre.
The queen must be covered — pocket one of your coins right after it.
Only your fingers may flick the striker — never touch the coins with your hands.
First to pocket all their coins wins.
fact: Carrom's cousins are played all over Asia, and champion players can sink a coin from across the board without seeming to aim at all.
